ai.title: Native app client events, admission status, and publish failure codes
ai.summary: The common package adds a new module, common/src/analytics/client-events.ts, that defines the wire contract for native iOS and Android app events ingested via the POST /api/v1/client-events endpoint, including per-event property schemas and a batch limit of 50 events. In parallel, the CLI admission flow now records a structured admission_status property on failed model requests, mapping session failures to tokens like request_timeout or paywall so telemetry distinguishes the cause of a refusal. The Sites publish subsystem gains a closed set of SITE_PUBLISH_FAILURE_CODES and a failure_code field on error results, letting analytics break down publish failures by reason instead of free-text messages. The product funnel schema also widens its surface enum to include ios and android, and new analytics event constants for mobile app opens, reviews, pushes, features, and crash reports are registered in the shared AnalyticsEvent enum.
ai.evidence: New file common/src/analytics/client-events.ts defines the wire contract for POST /api/v1/client-events with constants like CLIENT_EVENTS_MAX_EVENTS = 50. cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-chat-admission.ts adds sessionFailureStatus to map failures to admission_status, and common/src/sites/publish-events.ts introduces SITE_PUBLISH_FAILURE_CODES and failure_code fields.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side route that consumes POST /api/v1/client-events or the app code that emits these events, so rollout state of the mobile pipeline is not visible here.

Attaches a structured admission_status property to failed model admission events
Introduces SITE_PUBLISH_FAILURE_CODES and adds a failure_code field to publish error results
Extends product funnel and analytics schemas for mobile surfaces and new outcome events
Adds runId to the feedback request schema and mobile app version parsing to the client-platform utility

eli5.text: Freebuff now records detailed, fixed reasons for why requests get blocked, such as when a model is unavailable or a payment is required, so support and data teams can see exactly what happened instead of just a generic error. For website publishing, the system now logs specific, stable codes for why a deployment failed, distinguishing between issues like network problems or build errors. Additionally, the shared data system has been updated to recognize events coming from mobile phone apps, ensuring that activity from those devices is tracked accurately alongside desktop and web usage. These improvements are internal data refinements that help the team understand user behavior better, and they do not change how the application looks or behaves for you.

ai.title: Add personal summary style, Buffy mode, and integration guidance
ai.summary: Introduces a personal variant of the structured conversation summary, a new Buffy workspace mode, and a user-specific integrations prompt for shared-system-prompt agents. In packages/agent-runtime, a personal summary targets 3000 tokens, reads the model's reply by its '## Standing Requests' first heading, and keeps the newest whole turns word-for-word in a 4000-token tail via applyConversationSummary tailTokens. The common desktop-cloud contract adds a buffy field to CloudHistoryChat and narrows project mode to 'code' or 'chat', while the new integrationsGuidance and integrationsConnectedStatus functions let a fixed root agent's prompt reference a user's connected apps without naming them.

ai.title: MacOS window button placement added to desktop workspace
ai.summary: The `HostedWorkspaceHost` contract in `common` gains an optional `buttons` field on the `window` capability for macOS desktop builds. This allows the hosted renderer to place the native window controls, which are not scaled by the interface size, by specifying their center point and span. The feature is gated to newer Desktop builds that support this layout adjustment.

This internal update only affects people using the newest Mac desktop builds that support this specific feature. Until the desktop app is updated to actually use this new option, nothing changes in your daily use.
